channel.title: The Wartime Report
channel.description: Open source, unbiased, independent daily coverage of the 2026 Iran War. Military updates, economic impact, investigations.

item.title: Day 124 — Executive Privilege Showdown Looms as Subpoena Deadline Approaches
item.description: July 1, 2026: White House expected to invoke executive privilege within 48 hours after Senate subpoenas. Constitutional battle over war powers oversight intensifies as oil holds $72-73 range despite Hormuz demining progress. House prepares parallel subpoena resolution.

item.title: Day 123 — First Subpoenas Issued as Administration Defies Senate Oversight Demand
item.description: June 30, 2026: Senate Foreign Relations Committee issues first formal subpoenas to State Department officials after eleven days of silence on classified briefing. Administration signals executive privilege claim likely. Oil markets hold steady near $72-73 Brent range as Persian Gulf shipping normalizes ahead of full Hormuz reopening.

item.title: Day 122 — Senate Foreign Relations Votes to Authorize Subpoenas for Administration Officials
item.description: June 29, 2026: Senate Foreign Relations Committee authorizes subpoena power after ten days of administration silence on classified briefing demand. Armed Services constitutional authority hearing set for early July. Oil markets open Monday as Hormuz demining continues ahead of schedule.

item.title: Day 121 — Senate Prepares Subpoena Vote as Constitutional Authority Review Advances
item.description: June 28, 2026: Senate Foreign Relations Committee set for Monday subpoena authorization vote after nine days of administration silence. Armed Services Committee to hold parallel constitutional authority hearing in early July. Markets closed for weekend with Brent stabilized near $73 as Hormuz traffic reaches 75% of pre-war levels despite ceasefire violations.

item.title: Day 120 — Weekend Quiet as Senate Subpoena Vote Approaches
item.description: June 27, 2026: Weekend pause in developments as Senate Foreign Relations Committee prepares for Monday's subpoena authorization vote. Administration remained silent on eight-day-old briefing demand. Markets closed with oil stable near $73 as Hormuz traffic holds at 75% of pre-war levels.

item.title: Day 119 — Senate Foreign Relations Votes Monday on Subpoena Authorization
item.description: June 26, 2026: Senate Foreign Relations Committee scheduled subpoena authorization vote for Monday after seven days of administration silence on classified briefing demand. Armed Services Committee finalizing constitutional authority hearing schedule. Markets hold steady with Brent at $88-89.

item.title: Day 118 — Six Days Without Response as Senate Leadership Prepares Subpoena Vote
item.description: June 25, 2026: Administration silence reached sixth day on Senate briefing demand as Foreign Relations Committee scheduled preliminary subpoena vote for Monday. Armed Services joins constitutional authority challenge. State Department confirms no briefing scheduled despite 47-senator petition. Markets steady with Brent at $88-89.

item.title: Day 117 — Senate Moves Toward Subpoena Power as Administration Maintains Silence
item.description: June 24, 2026: With five days of silence on the 47-senator briefing demand, Senate Foreign Relations Committee leadership signals readiness to compel testimony. Legal authority challenge spreads to Armed Services Committee as bipartisan frustration over AUMF reliance intensifies. Trump-Netanyahu meeting remains unscheduled.

item.title: Day 116 — Administration Ignores 47-Senator Briefing Demand as Legal Authority Debate Intensifies
item.description: June 23, 2026: Four days after 47 senators demanded a classified briefing on Iran strategy, the administration remains silent. House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing revealed deep bipartisan split over war powers as reliance on 2001-2002 AUMFs faces mounting scrutiny. Trump-Netanyahu meeting postponed for third time.

item.title: Day 115 — House Foreign Affairs Hearing Exposes Deep Divide on War Authority
item.description: June 22, 2026: House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing reveals fracture over administration's legal authority for continued operations without renewed AUMF. Senate briefing demand still pending as Trump-Netanyahu meeting postponed for third time. Oil drifts to $88.50 as markets price diplomatic paralysis.

item.title: Day 114 — Senate Demands Briefing as Diplomatic Deadlock Enters Fourth Month
item.description: June 21, 2026: 47 senators demand classified briefing on administration's Iran strategy as peace talks remain stalled. Trump-Netanyahu meeting delayed again. Oil holds near $89 as markets price extended Hormuz disruption. Three core issues block progress.

item.title: Day 113 — Diplomatic Stalemate Deepens with No Breakthrough in Sight
item.description: June 21, 2026: Trump-Netanyahu meeting delayed until next week leaves peace talks in limbo. Three core negotiating issues remain unresolved after nearly two weeks of deadlock. Oil markets stabilize as traders price in extended disruption.

item.title: Day 112 — Peace Talks Remain Deadlocked as Key Trump-Netanyahu Summit Pushed to Next Week
item.description: June 20, 2026: Diplomatic uncertainty deepens with postponed White House meeting. Three core issues remain unresolved. Oil markets stabilize near $89 as traders accept extended disruption.

item.title: Day 111 — Diplomatic Deadlock Deepens as Trump-Netanyahu Meeting Postponed
item.description: June 19, 2026: Three core issues remain unresolved in peace talks. Trump-Netanyahu meeting delayed until next week adds fresh uncertainty. Oil markets signal acceptance of extended Hormuz disruption.

item.title: Day 110 — Trump-Netanyahu Meeting Postponed as Three Core Issues Remain Unresolved
item.description: June 18, 2026: Peace talks deadlocked on enrichment caps, sanctions sequencing, and Gulf security. Oil markets stabilize at $89, suggesting extended disruption now priced in. Congressional pressure intensifies.

item.title: Day 109 — Diplomatic Stalemate Hardens, Congressional Pressure Mounts as Oil Stabilizes Near $89
item.description: June 17, 2026: Peace talks show no progress despite repeated claims of breakthrough. European divisions over Iran strategy deepen. Oil markets calm as traders adjust to extended disruption. Congress demands clarity on endgame.

item.title: Day 108 — Negotiations Deadlocked as Both Sides Harden Positions, Energy Markets Stabilize
item.description: June 16, 2026: Peace talks remain stalled despite public optimism. G7 divisions deepen over Iran strategy. Oil steady at $89/barrel as markets adjust to extended Hormuz disruption.

item.title: Day 107 — Peace Framework Stalls as G7 Splits on Iran Strategy, Hormuz Flows Hold Steady
item.description: June 15, 2026: G7 summit fractures over sanctions relief timing as Iran-US talks remain deadlocked. Oil markets calm at $89/barrel. Congressional Republicans demand clearer endgame from Trump administration.

item.title: Day 106 — G7 Summit Opens as Iran Peace Deal Remains Elusive, Oil Holds at $89
item.description: June 14, 2026: G7 leaders gather in France with Iran war topping agenda. Deal framework still incomplete despite optimistic signals. Hormuz flows stabilize at 50% of pre-war levels. Republicans question Trump's shifting strategy.

item.title: Day 105 — Deal Hopes Fade as Iran Calls US Terms Excessive, Oil Rebounds to $89
item.description: June 13, 2026: Iran's foreign minister says deal has 'never been closer' but excessive US demands threaten breakthrough. Oil rebounds to $89. Hormuz flows reach half pre-war levels. G7 summit begins Monday with Iran peace as priority.

item.title: Day 104 — Trump Claims Deal Breakthrough, Cancels Strikes as Iran Says Nothing Finalized
item.description: June 12, 2026: Trump claims deal breakthrough, cancels strikes. Saudi media reports draft deal includes 60-day truce, Hormuz reopening, sanctions relief. Iran says nothing finalized. US kills 3 Indian sailors in blockade strikes, India summons US diplomat. Oil slides to $85.91. Strategic reserves running out. G7 summit Monday.

item.title: Day 103 — Diplomatic Framework Talks Stall as Reserves Near Critical Threshold
item.description: June 11, 2026: Framework negotiation efforts showed no signs of breakthrough while U.S. strategic petroleum reserves approached depletion levels that could force fundamental policy changes. With oil past $115 and over 3,000 vessels still stranded near Hormuz, energy officials warned that continued drawdowns could exhaust remaining flexibility within weeks.

item.title: Day 102 — Strategic Reserve Depletion Raises Stakes as Oil Climbs Past $115
item.description: June 10, 2026: U.S. strategic petroleum reserves approach critical levels as diplomatic framework talks show no breakthrough. Oil prices climb past $115 per barrel while over 3,000 vessels remain stranded near Hormuz, deepening global economic strain and raising questions about the sustainability of current buffer strategies.

item.title: Day 101 — Economic Pressure Mounts as Diplomatic Talks Remain Stalled
item.description: June 9, 2026: With the 100-day milestone passed, global markets face mounting anxiety over extended Hormuz disruptions. Oil prices climb past $115/barrel as strategic reserves near critical depletion, while diplomatic framework negotiations show little progress on core sanctions and security issues.

item.title: Day 100 — One Hundred Days: No Resolution as Hormuz Crisis Deepens
item.description: June 8, 2026: The war enters its 100th day with no end in sight. Over 3,000 vessels remain stranded near the Strait of Hormuz as diplomatic efforts continue to stall over framework implementation details. Global markets brace for extended disruption.

item.title: Day 99 — Hormuz Shipping Gridlock Persists as Diplomatic Impasse Deepens
item.description: June 6, 2026: Over 3,000 vessels remain stranded near Strait of Hormuz as framework disputes continue to stall diplomatic progress. Markets show growing concerns that the standoff could persist well beyond initial expectations, with supply chain disruptions compounding inflation pressures.

item.title: Day 98 — Shipping Backlog Deepens as Diplomatic Deadlock Persists
item.description: June 5, 2026: Over 3,000 vessels remain stranded near Strait of Hormuz as framework disputes stall progress toward reopening. Oil markets hold near $97 Brent while Fed officials signal patience on rate cuts amid persistent energy inflation.

item.title: Day 97 — Markets Weigh Fed Policy as Diplomatic Framework Remains Elusive
item.description: June 4, 2026: Oil markets stabilize near $97 Brent as investors digest the growing divergence between US and Iranian negotiating positions. Fed policy expectations shift as persistent energy inflation complicates the path forward. European mediators work to bridge gaps between competing frameworks.

item.title: Day 96 — Diplomatic Uncertainty Deepens as Markets Digest Rubio's Rejection of Sanctions Relief
item.description: June 3, 2026: Global markets weigh the implications of Secretary Rubio's testimony that no sanctions will be lifted for Hormuz reopening, as both sides appear to be negotiating from different frameworks. Oil markets stabilize near $96 Brent while diplomatic channels attempt to bridge the widening gap between US and Iranian positions.

item.title: Day 95 — Markets Hit New Records as Oil Rebounds; Rubio Rejects Iran Sanctions Relief
item.description: June 2, 2026: S&P 500 tops 7,600 and Dow reaches all-time high as Marvell surges 32% on AI chip demand. Brent crude climbs to $96 as Secretary Rubio tells Senate no sanctions will be lifted for Hormuz reopening, contradicting Iranian accounts and weakening the deal framework.

item.title: Day 94 — Western Powers Weigh Response to Iran's Conditional Peace Terms
item.description: June 1, 2026: Major powers deliberate whether to accept Iran's amended ratification or demand clean approval as the May 31 deadline passes without immediate resolution, with diplomatic channels focused on bridging gaps between Tehran's security guarantee requirements and Western insistence on unconditional implementation.

item.title: Day 93 — Deadline Arrives as P5+1 Review Iran's Conditional Terms
item.description: May 31, 2026: The P5+1 deadline arrives with major powers weighing whether to accept Iran's conditional ratification of the peace framework or demand clean approval, as Tehran's added security guarantee requirements complicate final implementation.

item.title: Day 92 — Parliament Ratifies Peace Framework With Conditions
item.description: May 30, 2026: Iran's parliament narrowly approved the peace framework with conditional amendments requiring P5+1 guarantees, setting up a final diplomatic scramble before tomorrow's deadline as hardliners secured partial victory in the ratification vote.

item.title: Day 91 — Parliament Votes: Ratification Showdown Begins
item.description: May 29, 2026: Iran's parliament convenes for the most consequential vote of the war — ratification of the peace framework that could end three months of conflict or collapse under hardliner amendments with just two days before the May 31 deadline.

item.title: Day 90 — 24 Hours to Vote: Parliament Braces for Ratification Showdown
item.description: May 28, 2026: With just one day until Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf's scheduled vote, moderate MPs make final appeals while hardliners threaten amendments that could collapse the peace framework hours before the May 31 P5+1 deadline expires.

item.title: Day 89 — Four Days to Vote: Diplomatic Pressure Mounts as Hardliners Prepare Amendments
item.description: May 27, 2026: With the May 29 ratification vote just 48 hours away, moderate MPs scramble for votes while hardliners draft last-minute amendments demanding written sanctions guarantees that could derail the entire peace framework before the May 31 P5+1 deadline expires.

item.title: Day 88 — Five Days to Deadline: Iran's Parliament Sets Final Vote for May 29
item.description: May 26, 2026: Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf scheduled the final ratification vote for May 29, giving lawmakers and the P5+1 just 48 hours before the May 31 diplomatic deadline expires with Iran's parliamentary process set to deliver a verdict two days before time runs out.

item.title: Day 87 — Iran's Parliament Votes to Advance P5+1 Framework as Deadline Clock Ticks
item.description: May 25, 2026: Iran's Majlis passed a procedural vote sending the P5+1 peace framework to full parliamentary debate, clearing the first formal hurdle as both sides race against a May 31 diplomatic deadline with just six days remaining.

item.title: Day 86 — Ghalibaf Schedules First Procedural Vote as 7-Day Deadline Looms
item.description: May 24, 2026: Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf announced a procedural vote on the P5+1 framework for Sunday, May 25, following a week of intense backroom negotiations, as Iran enters the final seven days before the May 31 diplomatic deadline with moderate MPs warning that any further delays could cause the entire framework to collapse.

item.title: Day 85 — Parliament Deadlock Enters Seventh Day With No Vote Scheduled
item.description: May 23, 2026: Iran's Majlis entered a seventh day of debate on the P5+1 peace framework with Speaker Ghalibaf still refusing to set a vote date, as hardliners demanded written guarantees and reformists warned amendments could collapse the deal entirely with just 8 days until the May 31 diplomatic deadline.

item.title: Day 84 — Parliamentary Deadlock Drags Into Sixth Day
item.description: May 22, 2026: Iran's parliament entered a sixth day of debate on the P5+1 enforcement framework with no vote scheduled, as hardliners and reformists remained divided on sanctions relief language, narrowing the window before the May 31 diplomatic deadline.

item.title: Day 83 — Parliament Extends Review as Diplomatic Deadline Nears
item.description: May 21, 2026: Iran's parliament entered a fifth day of review on the P5+1 enforcement framework as hardliners continued demanding textual amendments on sanctions relief timelines, extending uncertainty as the informal May 31 diplomatic deadline approaches.

item.title: Day 82 — Parliament Review Extends Into Fourth Day as Hardliners Demand Text Changes
item.description: May 20, 2026: Iran's parliamentary review of the P5+1 enforcement framework entered its fourth day with the conservative bloc shifting from procedural objections to demanding specific textual amendments on sanctions relief and verification timelines.

item.title: Day 81 — Conservative Bloc Pushes Framework Amendments as Review Drags On
item.description: May 19, 2026: Iran's hardline conservatives demanded amendments to the P5+1 framework during day three of parliamentary review, extending the approval timeline as oil markets showed renewed volatility.

item.title: Day 80 — Hardliners Demand Guarantees as Parliament Review Enters Second Day
item.description: May 18, 2026: Iran's parliamentary review of the P5+1 framework entered its second day as conservative factions intensified demands for binding sanctions relief commitments and verification protocol safeguards before any acceptance vote.

item.title: Day 79 — Iran's Parliament Begins Framework Debate as Supreme Leader Demands Guarantees
item.description: May 17, 2026: Iran's Islamic Consultative Assembly opened formal review of the P5+1 enforcement framework while hardliners demanded ironclad guarantees on sanctions relief and verification protocols before accepting terms.

item.title: Day 78 — Implementation Phase Begins as Iran Reviews Framework Terms
item.description: May 16, 2026: Following P5+1 ratification, Iran began formal review of enforcement framework as sanctions relief timeline was outlined and IAEA verification teams prepared for deployment under the newly binding international commitment.

item.title: Day 77 — P5+1 Vote Ratifies Enforcement Framework as Ceasefire Path Solidifies
item.description: May 15, 2026: P5+1 foreign ministers formally ratified the enforcement framework in a landmark vote that transformed diplomatic momentum into binding commitment, clearing the pathway toward ending the 77-day war through negotiated settlement.

item.title: Day 76 — P5+1 Ministers Schedule Ratification Vote as Framework Gains Momentum
item.description: May 14, 2026: Following Tehran's framework acceptance, P5+1 foreign ministers scheduled a formal ratification vote as the enforcement mechanism moved from technical consensus to binding political commitment. Diplomatic momentum accelerated toward ending the 76-day war.

item.title: Day 75 — Iran Accepts P5+1 Framework as Ministers Move to Ratification Vote
item.description: May 13, 2026: Tehran formally accepted enforcement framework contingent on sanctions timeline. P5+1 ministers scheduled ratification vote as diplomatic momentum accelerated toward binding agreement. Snap-back mechanism finalized after Vienna consultations.

item.title: Day 74 — P5+1 Ministers Schedule Framework Vote as Iran Signals Conditional Acceptance
item.description: May 12, 2026: P5+1 enforcement framework advanced to formal vote after ministerial consensus. Tehran indicated potential acceptance contingent on sanctions relief timeline. Snap-back mechanism language finalized after Vienna consultations as diplomatic momentum accelerated.

item.title: Day 73 — P5+1 Framework Vote Advances as First IAEA Teams Complete Initial Site Assessments
item.description: May 11, 2026: Enforcement framework moved toward final political approval as IAEA inspection teams completed first round of verification assessments under new protocols. Snap-back mechanism language neared consensus after Vienna consultations.

item.title: Day 72 — IAEA Inspection Teams Deploy Across Iran as Enforcement Framework Nears Final Vote
item.description: May 10, 2026: First IAEA inspection teams began deployment under new verification protocols as P5+1 ministers in Vienna worked toward final approval of enforcement mechanisms. Compliance systems entered active implementation phase, building on yesterday's ministerial summit.

item.title: Day 71 — P5+1 Foreign Ministers Convene in Vienna as Final Framework Vote Approaches
item.description: May 9, 2026: With enforcement framework text nearly finalized, P5+1 foreign ministers opened high-level consultations in Vienna. IAEA technical deployment continued as ministerial summit works toward final political approval of compliance mechanisms.

item.title: Day 70 — Ministerial Summit Scheduled as Framework Text Nears Final Vote
item.description: May 8, 2026: With enforcement framework language nearly finalized, P5+1 foreign ministers will convene in Vienna next week for final political consultations. IAEA technical teams received deployment authorization as verification protocols entered implementation phase.

item.title: Day 69 — Enforcement Framework Text Near Completion as Technical Teams Set Implementation Roadmap
item.description: May 7, 2026: Building on yesterday's hybrid sanctions mechanism breakthrough, P5+1 teams worked through consolidated compliance language while IAEA technical experts finalized sampling deployment schedules and threshold definitions for the agreed enforcement triggers.

item.title: Day 68 — Sanctions Snap-Back Compromise Emerges as P5+1 Narrows Enforcement Gap
item.description: May 6, 2026: Negotiators report breakthrough on hybrid sanctions mechanism combining automatic triggers with Security Council oversight. Technical teams advance implementation timelines while political divisions narrow on compliance framework.

item.title: Day 67 — P5+1 Edges Toward Compromise Framework as Sanctions Trigger Deadlock Persists
item.description: May 5, 2026: Following yesterday's finalized sampling protocols, negotiators narrow gap on enforcement language while automatic sanctions triggers remain the key sticking point. Western and Chinese delegations report progress but no breakthrough.

item.title: Day 66 — Sampling Protocols Finalized as P5+1 Narrows Enforcement Mechanism Gap
item.description: May 4, 2026: IAEA and Iranian officials reach agreement on enrichment monitoring procedures while Western and Chinese negotiators make progress on compliance framework language, though automatic sanctions triggers remain unresolved.

item.title: Day 65 — IAEA Teams Complete Initial Facility Assessments, Verification Framework Advances
item.description: May 3, 2026: International inspectors finalize baseline protocols at Iranian enrichment sites as managed-access framework takes operational shape, marking substantive progress toward comprehensive verification architecture despite unresolved enforcement mechanism disputes.

item.title: Day 64 — Tehran Opens Nuclear Facilities as Verification Protocol Takes Shape
item.description: May 2, 2026: Iranian authorities grant preliminary access to enrichment sites as IAEA inspection teams complete initial facility assessments and establish managed-access protocols while P5+1 enforcement mechanism negotiations continue amid Chinese framework pressure.

item.title: Day 63 — IAEA Inspection Teams Deploy to Tehran as Framework Timeline Accelerates
item.description: May 1, 2026: International Atomic Energy Agency advance inspection teams arrive in Tehran to begin technical verification protocol implementation while P5+1 partners work to finalize enforcement mechanism language amid accelerating diplomatic timeline and competing Chinese mediation framework.

item.title: Day 62 — P5+1 Partners Convene as IAEA Verification Framework Takes Shape
item.description: April 30, 2026: P5+1 partners begin multilateral coordination meetings while IAEA technical teams advance managed-access inspection protocols, though Chinese alternative framework remains under development amid competing diplomatic initiatives.

item.title: Day 61 — IAEA Begins Inspection Talks as Washington Reviews Timeline Flexibility
item.description: April 29, 2026: International Atomic Energy Agency opens technical consultations on managed-access verification protocols while White House policy review examines Franco-German twelve-year framework as potential basis for multilateral agreement.

item.title: Day 60 — European Framework Emerges as Tehran Tests Verification Boundaries
item.description: April 28, 2026: France and Germany unveil joint twelve-year enrichment framework merging IAEA verification protocols with Turkish duration proposal as Iran conducts underground centrifuge tests while signaling conditional flexibility on inspection access timelines.

item.title: Day 59 — Verification Protocol Negotiations Intensify as Economic Pressure Mounts
item.description: April 27, 2026: European mediators work to integrate Turkish twelve-year enrichment proposal with enhanced IAEA verification protocols as White House signals flexibility on duration in exchange for robust snap-back mechanisms while Tehran adapts to foreign currency depletion through unconventional financing and barter arrangements.

item.title: Day 58 — Diplomatic Framework Advances as Tehran Economic Deadline Passes
item.description: April 26, 2026: Turkish twelve-year enrichment timeline gains traction among European mediators as Iran's foreign currency reserves cross historically critical depletion threshold without triggering immediate policy shift while verification protocol negotiations intensify across multiple diplomatic channels.

item.title: Day 57 — Turkey Proposes Twelve-Year Enrichment Timeline as Tehran Economic Clock Winds Down
item.description: April 25, 2026: Turkish mediation presents ten-to-twelve year uranium enrichment suspension compromise as Iran's foreign currency reserves enter final seventy-two hours before historically critical depletion threshold while European diplomatic channel gains momentum with modified verification framework proposals.

item.title: Day 56 — Blockade Enters Second Week as Iran's Reserves Near Critical Levels
item.description: April 24, 2026: US naval blockade completes eleventh day with Iran's foreign currency reserves approaching historically critical depletion threshold, while trilateral mediation efforts continue to seek compromise on enrichment suspension timelines amid growing signs of domestic economic pressure within Tehran.

item.title: Day 55 — Naval Blockade Strains Iran's Economy as Mediation Efforts Stall
item.description: April 23, 2026: US naval blockade enters tenth day with Iran's oil revenues completely frozen and diplomatic talks deadlocked over enrichment timelines, pushing both sides deeper into economic standoff with no breakthrough in sight despite continued trilateral mediation from Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey.

item.title: Day 54 — US Naval Blockade Enters Second Week as Economic Pressure Mounts on Tehran
item.description: April 22, 2026: US naval blockade of Iranian ports continues to strangle Tehran's economy as diplomatic efforts remain deadlocked over enrichment timelines and sovereignty disputes, with both sides dug in despite mounting economic costs that have now exceeded $750 million in frozen Iranian oil revenues.

item.title: Day 53 — Blockade Economic Toll Tops $700 Million as Diplomatic Mediation Stalls
item.description: April 21, 2026: US naval blockade of Iranian ports enters second week with Iran's oil export revenue completely frozen, pushing cumulative economic losses past $700 million as pressure mounts on both sides to accept modified mediation frameworks that remain deadlocked over uranium enrichment timelines and sovereignty concessions.

item.title: Day 52 — Blockade Enters Seventh Day as Diplomatic Push Accelerates
item.description: April 20, 2026: US naval blockade continues for seventh consecutive day with total Iranian oil export shutdown. Economic losses surpass $600 million as Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey intensify mediation efforts to bridge enrichment gap that remains core obstacle.

item.title: Day 51 — Blockade Enters Sixth Day as Economic Pressure Intensifies
item.description: April 19, 2026: US naval blockade continues for sixth consecutive day with zero Iranian oil exports. Economic toll surpasses $500 million in lost revenue as markets brace for potential breakthrough or prolonged stalemate. Diplomatic channels remain active but enrichment gap appears unbridgeable.

item.title: Day 50 — Diplomatic Deadlock Deepens as Blockade Enters Fifth Day
item.description: April 18, 2026: US naval blockade continues with zero commercial activity at Iranian ports. Enrichment cap rejection stalls Pakistan-led peace framework. Oil holds above $100 as markets price in extended standoff. Economic pressure mounting but Tehran shows no signs of compromise.

item.title: Day 49 — Framework Stalls as Iran Rejects Enrichment Cap
item.description: April 17, 2026: Pakistan-led ceasefire proposal hits impasse over uranium enrichment limits. US naval blockade continues into fourth day with zero Iranian shipping activity. Oil trades in narrow range as markets await diplomatic breakthrough or renewed escalation.

item.title: Day 48 — Blockade Holds as Mediators Push New Framework
item.description: April 16, 2026: US naval blockade enters third day with diplomatic momentum building. Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey present revised ceasefire proposal as markets digest prolonged standoff. Oil consolidates above $99, defense stocks resilient, Trump signals conditional willingness to negotiate.

item.title: Day 47 — Naval Blockade Day Two: Markets Stabilize as Diplomacy Resumes
item.description: April 15, 2026: US naval blockade enters second day with minimal shipping activity. Markets digest ceasefire collapse as Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey renew mediation efforts. Oil holds above $99, defense stocks resilient, Trump weighs next moves.

item.title: Day 46 — Blockade Tightens as Markets Hold Rally, Oil Steady Near $100
item.description: April 14, 2026: US naval blockade enters second day as markets digest yesterday's dramatic reversal. Oil holds near $100, defense stocks resilient, Trump weighs next moves as diplomatic channels remain open.

item.title: Day 45 — Markets Erase War Losses Despite Naval Blockade
item.description: April 13, 2026: S&P 500 closes at highest level since before the war as Trump orders naval blockade of Iranian ports after Islamabad peace talks collapse. Oil surges back above $100.

item.title: Day 44 — Islamabad Talks Stall on Hormuz Control as Israel-Lebanon Fighting Continues
item.description: April 13, 2026: Mediators struggle to bridge gap between Iran's demand for sovereign control over Strait and US insistence on free navigation. Lebanon front threatens to unravel fragile ceasefire as Netanyahu refuses to halt operations. Markets whipsaw on diplomatic uncertainty.

item.title: Day 43 — Islamabad Peace Talks Begin as Ceasefire Hangs by a Thread
item.description: April 11, 2026: Regional mediators convene in Islamabad for first formal negotiations as two-week ceasefire shows signs of strain. Hormuz passage remains minimal, Israel-Lebanon tensions unresolved, markets whipsaw on fragile diplomatic hopes.

item.title: Day 42 — Ceasefire Fragile on Day Two as Hormuz Remains Closed, Israel-Lebanon Tensions Threaten Deal
item.description: April 10, 2026: Two-week ceasefire holds but tensions mount. Iran accuses US of violations. Strait of Hormuz functionally closed despite agreement. Netanyahu excludes Lebanon from ceasefire, Pakistan disagrees. Markets whipsaw as oil rebounds, energy stocks fall.

item.title: Day 41 — Islamabad Accords Ceasefire Triggers Historic Market Surge, Oil Crashes 16%
item.description: April 9, 2026: Two-week ceasefire declared. Oil crashes 16% in largest single-day drop since 2020. Dow surges 1,325 points. Hormuz reopening uncertain as IRGC maintains control. Energy stocks hammered while airlines, travel stocks soar on peace premium.

item.title: Day 40 — Missing US Pilot Recovered Alive as Trump's Hormuz Deadline Triggers Massive Escalation
item.description: April 8, 2026: US rescue forces extract missing F-15E crew member after three-day manhunt. Trump's Monday deadline expired, triggering new wave of strikes. Iran retaliates with largest missile barrage yet. Oil prices surge past $115/barrel as Hormuz remains closed.

item.title: Day 39 — Islamabad Accords: Two-Week Ceasefire Declared
item.description: April 7, 2026: Trump accepts Pakistan-brokered two-week ceasefire. Iran agrees to reopen Strait of Hormuz under IRGC management. Peace negotiations to begin Friday in Islamabad.

item.title: Day 38 — Trump Deadline Passes as Pakistan Brokers Extension
item.description: April 6, 2026: Pakistan Prime Minister requests two-week extension of Trump's Hormuz deadline. Kharg Island strikes already underway before deadline expires.

item.title: Day 37 — Race to Find Missing US Pilot as Trump's Monday Deadline Looms
item.description: April 5, 2026: One F-15E crew member still missing after Friday's shoot-down. Iran offering rewards for his capture. Trump's 48-hour Hormuz ultimatum expires Monday. Nuclear plant struck. Two US aircraft lost in worst day since Iraq War.

item.title: Day 36 — Two US Aircraft Shot Down in Single Day as Iran Proves Air Defenses Intact
item.description: April 4, 2026: F-15E Strike Eagle and A-10 Warthog lost to hostile fire — worst US aviation day since early Iraq War. One crew member still missing in Iran. Search-and-rescue helicopters also damaged. Trump deadline 2 days away.

item.title: Day 35 — World Bypasses Washington as Coalition Forms to Reopen Hormuz
item.description: April 3, 2026: UN Security Council to vote on Hormuz resolution Saturday as China opposes force. Iran claims second F-35 shot down, puts Gulf bridges on hit list. US intel warns Iran can still 'wreak absolute havoc.' Trump deadline 3 days away.

item.title: Day 34 — 40 Nations Meet to Reopen Hormuz as Trump Tells Allies "Not Our Problem"
item.description: April 2, 2026: 40 countries convene without the US to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Asian markets tank after Trump's prime-time address offers no plan. Oil spikes 5%+. IEA warns April crunch worse than March. Iran sets up Hormuz toll booth. Israel intensifies Lebanon attacks.

item.title: Day 33 — Trump Abandons Four Decades of Gulf Policy, Says Hormuz "Not Our Problem"
item.description: April 1, 2026: Trump declares US will leave Iran 'in two or three weeks' and keeping Strait of Hormuz open is not America's responsibility — reversing 40+ years of US Gulf doctrine. NATO shoots down Iranian missile over Turkey. IRGC threatens 18 US tech companies. Brent crude volatile as markets digest policy chaos.

item.title: Day 32 — Iranian Drone Strikes Kuwaiti Oil Tanker at Dubai Port as Gulf Leaders Meet in Jeddah
item.description: March 31, 2026: Iranian drone strikes fully-laden Kuwaiti tanker Al-Salmi at Dubai port — fire and oil spill warning. Saudi, Qatar, Jordan leaders meet in Jeddah. Brent crude up 62% in March. EU emergency energy meeting today. April 6 Hormuz ultimatum 6 days away.

item.title: Day 31 — Marines Arrive for Ground War as IRGC's University Deadline Passes
item.description: March 30, 2026: Trump threatens to 'obliterate' Kharg Island, oil wells, and desalination plants if no deal reached. Spain closes airspace to US military. Brent past $116, up 55% in March. IAEA confirms Khondab destroyed. April 6 Hormuz ultimatum seven days away.

item.title: Day 30 — Houthis Enter War as Trump's April 6 Deadline Looms
item.description: March 29, 2026: Yemen's Houthis launch first strikes on Israel after Iran's nuclear sites hit. Trump's Hormuz ultimatum expires in 9 days. Oil hits $112. One month into conflict with no end in sight.

item.title: Day 29 — Iran's "Heavy Price" Retaliation After Nuclear Facility Strikes
item.description: March 28, 2026: Iran responds after Israel's unprecedented strikes on two nuclear sites. Trump's April 6 deadline looms. US casualty count rises past 300. Hormuz blockade enters fifth week.

item.title: Day 28 — Trump Extends Hormuz Deadline to April 6 as Iran Calls Peace Plan 'One-Sided'
item.description: March 27, 2026: Israel claims strikes on two Iranian nuclear sites. Iran vows 'heavy' retaliation. Rubio: 'weeks not months,' no ground troops needed. Brent crude hits $111. Iran death toll: 3,300+. Cargo through Hormuz down 50%.

item.title: Day 27 — Israel Kills Hormuz Blockade Mastermind as Iran Rejects US Peace Plan
item.description: March 26, 2026: Israel kills IRGC Navy commander Alireza Tangsiri in Bandar Abbas — architect of the Hormuz blockade. Iran rejects US 15-point peace plan. Trump extends energy deadline 10 days. Brent crude surges to $108.

item.title: Day 26 — Iran Dismisses Trump's Peace Claims as Strikes Hit Tehran
item.description: March 25, 2026: Trump declares war has been won while Tehran dismisses all claims of negotiations. 82nd Airborne deploying. Oil plunges 6% to $94 on peace signals. 12 killed in Tehran strikes.

item.title: Day 25 — US Sends 15-Point Peace Plan to Iran as Bushehr Nuclear Plant Hit
item.description: March 24, 2026: US sends 15-point peace plan via Pakistan, Bushehr nuclear plant struck, Trump declares 'we've won this war,' 1000+ more troops approved.

item.title: Day 24 — Trump Blinks: Ultimatum Extended 5 Days Amid 'Very Good' Iran Talks
item.description: March 23, 2026: Trump extends Hormuz ultimatum by 5 days, halts US strikes on Iran's energy sites, claims 'very good and productive conversations' with Iran. Iranian state TV declares 'US president backs down.' Tehran rocked by explosions. Iran fires missiles and drones at Bahrain. Brent at $112. Kremlin warns against nuclear plant strikes.

item.title: Day 23 — 48-Hour Ultimatum: Trump Threatens to Obliterate Iran's Power Grid
item.description: March 22, 2026: Trump issues 48-hour ultimatum — reopen Hormuz or US will 'obliterate' Iran's power plants. Iran strikes near Dimona nuclear facility. Israel's air defense fails to stop 2 missile strikes. Nuclear escalation fears mount.

item.title: Day 22 — Trump Hints at 'Winding Down' as Iran Strikes Diego Garcia
item.description: March 21, 2026: Iran fires ballistic missiles at Diego Garcia. Trump hints at 'winding down' but rules out ceasefire. Death toll reaches 1,444. Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi refinery hit. Saudi Arabia expels Iranian diplomats.

item.title: Day 21 — Three Weeks of War, No End in Sight
item.description: March 20, 2026: Iran warns of 'zero restraint.' Trump calls NATO allies 'cowards.' Switzerland halts US arms exports. Netanyahu signals possible ground invasion of Iran. Lebanon death toll tops 1,000.

item.title: Day 20 — Israel Strikes South Pars, Qatar LNG Crippled
item.description: March 19, 2026: Israel strikes South Pars gas field unilaterally. Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG facility hit — 17% of output cut for up to 5 years. Iran retaliates against Israeli oil refinery in Haifa.

item.title: Day 19 — War's Human Cost Hits Home
item.description: March 18, 2026: Three Palestinian women killed in beauty salon by Iranian missile shrapnel. Thai worker killed in Israel. The war's civilian toll spreads far beyond the battlefield.

item.title: Day 18 — Ali Larijani Killed, Israel Invades Lebanon
item.description: March 17, 2026: Ali Larijani, Iran's de facto leader after Khamenei's death, killed in strike. Israel launches limited ground invasion of Lebanon. Basij militia chief also killed.

item.title: Day 17 — U.S. Refueling Plane Crashes in Iraq
item.description: March 16, 2026: A U.S. refueling aircraft crashes in Iraq. The war's logistical strain begins to show as the air campaign enters its third week.

item.title: Day 16 — The Quiet Before the Storm
item.description: March 15, 2026: A brief operational lull as both sides regroup. Diplomatic channels remain frozen. The humanitarian crisis deepens across the region.

item.title: Day 15 — Isfahan Hit, Majority of Americans Oppose the War
item.description: March 14, 2026: Isfahan struck, killing at least 15. 53% of U.S. voters oppose the attacks. Israel running critically low on missile interceptors. Iran death toll passes 1,400.

item.title: Day 14 — Kharg Island Struck
item.description: March 13, 2026: U.S. forces strike Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub. Trump says he might 'hit it a few more times just for fun.' Iran threatens U.S. 'hideouts' in UAE.

item.title: Day 13 — Press Crackdown and Embassy Evacuations
item.description: March 12, 2026: Trump administration threatens news outlets over critical coverage. US tells citizens to leave Iraq after second embassy attack. European leaders refuse Hormuz involvement.

item.title: Day 12 — The War's Staggering Cost Comes Into Focus
item.description: March 11, 2026: Pentagon reveals $11.3 billion spent in first six days. IEA calls the Iran war the 'greatest energy security threat in history.' Trump searches for an endgame.

item.title: Day 11 — $11.3 Billion Spent as Trump Searches for Endgame
item.description: March 10, 2026: Pentagon reveals $11.3 billion spent in six days. Oil trade paralyzed. US tells citizens to leave Iraq. Trump admin threatens media outlets.

item.title: Day 10 — Mojtaba Khamenei Named Supreme Leader
item.description: March 9, 2026: Iran's Assembly of Experts names Mojtaba Khamenei as new supreme leader — the candidate Trump declared 'unacceptable.' Seventh US service member dies.

item.title: Day 9 — Oil Infrastructure Targeted for First Time
item.description: March 8, 2026: US and Israel strike Iranian oil depots for the first time. Massive fire at Shahran depot near Tehran. First Israeli soldiers killed. Assembly of Experts hints at successor.

item.title: Day 8 — One Week of War: 3,000 Targets, $3.7 Billion, 1,332 Dead
item.description: March 7, 2026: CENTCOM reports 3,000+ targets struck and 43 warships destroyed. Brent crude up 27% in one week. First US caskets arrive home. Norway embassy blast.

item.title: Day 7 — Hotel Bombings and a Growing Refugee Crisis
item.description: March 6, 2026: Israel bombs a Beirut hotel targeting Quds Force commanders. UK pledges military support to Saudi Arabia. Lebanon displacement crisis deepens.

item.title: Day 6 — Trump Demands Role in Choosing Iran's Next Leader
item.description: March 5, 2026: Trump tells Axios he wants to choose Khamenei's successor. Declares Mojtaba Khamenei 'unacceptable.' Demands unconditional surrender.

item.title: Day 5 — Congress Backs Trump as Iran Escalates
item.description: March 4, 2026: Congress rejects war powers resolutions. Hegseth says US 'just getting started.' Trump promises quadrupled weapons production.

item.title: Day 4 — Israel Strikes Assembly of Experts Meeting Site
item.description: March 3, 2026: Israel destroys the building where Iran's Assembly of Experts was to meet, preventing selection of a new supreme leader. Lebanon evacuations begin.

item.title: Day 3 — Hezbollah Enters the War
item.description: March 2, 2026: Hezbollah breaks its ceasefire and launches missiles into Israel from southern Lebanon. A Hezbollah drone strikes a British RAF base in Cyprus.

item.title: Day 2 — Dubai Airport Hit as Iran Strikes Back
item.description: March 1, 2026: Iran retaliates across Gulf states. Dubai International Airport damaged by drone strikes. Trump hints at Venezuela-style outcome.

item.title: Day 1 — Operation Epic Fury Begins
item.description: February 28, 2026: The United States and Israel launch nearly 900 strikes on Iran in 12 hours. Supreme Leader Khamenei killed. Operation Epic Fury begins.
